business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

stage_1.virtual_office_permissibility: A Swiss AG must maintain an actual registered office (Sitz) at a street address in Switzerland where process can be served and public documents are kept. A registered agent or business-centre address is accepted, but pure 'virtual office' with no administrative presence may be rejected or lead to re-characterization of tax residence; specific furnishing and substance guidance (e.g., actual mailbox, authorization to use premises) must be documented.
stage_1.physical_inspection_likelihood: 18-25% within the first three financial years where the company is domiciled at a shared business centre and claims Swiss VAT refunds; low physical inspection risk for a pure online DTC retail operation without inventory in Switzerland, but commercial register and tax authorities retain the right to verify economic substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), Articles 620-763 concerning the Aktiengesellschaft; Articles 940-950 concerning the Commercial Register; Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung) and the Swiss Business Name Index (Zefix) regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the canton of the registered office, operating under the supervisory authority of the Swiss Federal Department of Justice (FOJ) and coordinated via the Zefix national registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde) executed before a Swiss notary, accompanied by the Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts), filed for entry in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000; at least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be fully paid in at incorporation, with the aggregate paid-up amount not less than CHF 50,000. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked/escrow share-capital account with a licensed Swiss bank and evidenced by a capital confirmation certificate; contributions in kind require an audit report and confirmation of free disposal in accordance with Swiss Code of Obligations Article 635.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation deed and Articles of Association, executed before the Cantonal Notary, be and are hereby ratified and adopted in full. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 nominal value each, be and is hereby subscribed, and that the Board confirm deposit of CHF 50,000 into the blocked share-capital account held with a licensed Swiss bank, as evidenced by the bank capital confirmation. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at the address stated in the Articles of Association in the Canton of Zurich. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chairman of the Board of Directors, each accepting office with signatory authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Notariat / Etude notariale) in the canton of the registered office (e.g., Zurich)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the Swiss notary to draft and execute the public deed of incorporation together with the Articles of Association, covering the corporate name, registered office address, precise corporate purpose (online retail of cosmetics), authorized share capital, share classes, board composition, signatory authority, and auditor appointment terms. All incorporating shareholders and designated board members must sign in person before the notary; the notary verifies identities and legal capacity. The deed and articles must be drafted in an official Swiss language (German, French, or Italian).
required_dossiers: Passports or certified identity cards of all incorporators and directors
Draft corporate purpose mapping to ISIC 4791/NAICS 456120
Written declarations of acceptance from board members and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or reviewing authority queries a clause, the articles are amended by a corrective notarial deed and re-executed; any formal or capacity defect is cured through rectification before the same notary before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-Up Share Capital in Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank operating as an escrow institution (e.g., cantonal bank, UBS, ZKB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital formation escrow account in the name of the company to be incorporated and transfer the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000. Instruct the bank to issue, after clearing of funds and completion of KYC/AML checks, a Capital Confirmation Certificate (Kapitalbestätigung) addressed to the Commercial Register Office, confirming that the funds are irrevocably placed and at the free disposal of the company upon its registration. The account remains blocked until the Commercial Register entry is legally completed.
required_dossiers: Beneficial owner identification and KYC/AML forms
Corporate resolution confirming capital deposit instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence documents, provide certified bank statements and beneficial ownership declarations; once the KYC file is closed, the capital confirmation certificate is reissued within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Entry in the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the registered office canton, submitted through the Zefix electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the registration application signed by the board of directors, attaching the notarized incorporation deed, the Articles of Association, the bank capital confirmation, the board and auditor declarations, and the name search clearance. The commercial registrar verifies the uniqueness of the corporate name, the legality of the purpose, the adequacy of paid-up capital, and the qualifications of the officers. The company acquires separate legal personality upon entry in the register.
required_dossiers: Capital confirmation certificate from the Swiss bank
List of board members with certified signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to supplementary enquiries within 30 calendar days; if the name conflicts or the capital certificate is defective, amend and refile; a formal refusal may be appealed to the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority within 30 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt / Feuille officielle suisse du commerce), a federal publication organ managed by the Confederation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registration entry, the Commercial Register automatically transmits company data to the SHAB for mandatory electronic publication of incorporation, including company name, legal form (AG), registered office, corporate purpose, issued capital, officers, signatory powers, and registration date. The company's authorized representative must verify the published record against the register excerpt and maintain documentary proof for banks, counterparties, and tax authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any typographical discrepancy in the SHAB notice is corrected by filing a rectification request with the Commercial Register; the registry will republish the corrected data at no additional statutory charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security, and Occupational Accident Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Office; Federal Tax Administration (FTA/EStV); Central Compensation Office (ZAS/AHV-AVS); Suva occupational accident insurance authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the formed company with the cantonal tax authority for corporate income and net wealth tax purposes; register with the Federal Tax Administration for VAT if estimated annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, or voluntarily elect VAT registration to claim input tax credits; enroll as an employer with the AHV/IV compensation office for payroll deductions; and register employees with Suva for compulsory occupational and non-occupational accident insurance within 14 days of the first hiring.
required_dossiers: Commercial register excerpt and SHAB publication
Certified copy of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late submissions are remediated by voluntary self-disclosure and payment of any nominal penalty; objections to tax assessments may be raised with the cantonal administration within 30 days, and social security disputes are lodged with the competent compensation office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cosmetics Product Notification and Packaging Waste Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Office of Public Health (BAG) Cosmetics Notification Portal; Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (BLV); Swiss packaging recycling organizations (e.g., PRS Swiss Recycling) under the Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit each cosmetic product to be placed on the Swiss market through the BAG online notification portal, providing the product composition, packaging file, label texts, concentration limits, and the responsible person's identity; simultaneously declare packaging volumes to the Swiss Packaging Recycling scheme to satisfy extended producer responsibility obligations under the Swiss Packaging Ordinance. Maintain a safety assessment file per the Swiss Cosmetics Ordinance (VKOS) and cooperate with market surveillance authorities.
required_dossiers: Cosmetic product safety assessment per VKOS
Packaging volume declarations for PRS/FOEN compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BAG or BLV issues a correction request or market withdrawal notice, submit missing dossiers and revised notifications within 30 days; unresolved compliance issues are appealed to the Federal Administrative Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade Inspectorate (Gewerbepolizei / Inspectorat du commerce) and Federal Office of Public Health (BAG) for cosmetics market surveillance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating or manufacturing license is required for ISIC 4791 online retail of cosmetics (non-regulated retail trade). Mandatory notifications instead comprise the BAG cosmetics product notification under Article 28 of the Swiss Cosmetics Ordinance (VKOS) and the cantonal trade establishment notification (Gewerbeanmeldung) for the registered business premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt BAFU), acting together with the cantonal environmental protection authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 'B' notification is not triggered; pure retail warehousing and direct-to-consumer dispatch operations fall outside Annex 1 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVP/VIA), and no full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge from premises, including wash-down and sanitary flows, must meet municipal and cantonal limits under the Swiss Water Protection Act (GSchG) and its ordinances. Storage and dispatch of cosmetic products must not generate VOC emissions in excess of the thresholds under the Swiss Clean Air Ordinance (LRV). All sales packaging must comply with the Swiss Packaging Ordinance recycling quotas, and any hazardous aerosol or flammable personal care products must meet the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ChemRRV) handling and labeling standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cantonal Fire Prevention Authority (VKF/AFCB) is required where warehouse storage area exceeds 800 m² or where stored aerosols/inflammables reach hazardous threshold quantities; structural load inspections of storage shelving and racking must be certified by the cantonal building inspectorate in accordance with SIA standards; workplace compliance under the Swiss Occupational Safety and Health Act (ArG) is evidenced by a Suva accident insurance confirmation, first-aid provisions, temperature/ERG assessments, and employee safety instruction records before commencement of physical operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA), Division for VAT and Excise Duties; portal https://www.estv.admin.ch; UID portal https://www.uid.admin.ch; VAT e-services via https://www.estv.admin.ch/en/vat
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the Aktiengesellschaft with the Cantonal Commercial Register, including articles of association, capital confirmation and board resolutions; 2) The Commercial Register automatically grants the legal entity a UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / ID économique / identificatore d'impresa), which serves as the federal TIN; 3) For VAT, file form 035 'Registration for VAT' with ESTV or use the ESTV e-service after commercial registration, attaching the statutes, commercial register excerpt and projected turnover; 4) ESTV issues a separate VAT number in the format 'CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX MWST' for taxable entities; 5) The UID is used for income tax, federal and cantonal levies, social security and statistics.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or elective entity classification exists in Switzerland; taxation follows the statutory legal form. An Aktiengesellschaft is automatically subject to corporate income tax at federal, cantonal and communal level and to VAT at federal level. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Switzerland implements BEPS Action 2 through domestic anti-hybrid rules and its OECD MLI positions, without elective deduction or classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / MWST / TVA / IVA) under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual turnover from taxable supplies made in Switzerland (zero-rated exports count as taxable turnover for the threshold); voluntary registration from the first franc is available, particularly to recover input VAT. Foreign suppliers without a Swiss registered office must register if they generate at least CHF 100,000 from supplies to Swiss customers and do not benefit from an exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoice API clearance, or digital stamping regime. Invoices, whether paper or electronic, must contain the statutory content under Art. 26 VAT Act: supplier and recipient identification, type and volume of goods or services, date of supply, consideration, tax rate and tax amount. Tax-relevant electronic records must be archived and made available to ESTV for ten years. The QR-bill and eBill standards are common but not compulsory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Switzerland to a foreign destination qualify for the zero rate under Art. 23 VAT Act when the removal from Swiss customs territory is proven by a customs export declaration or equivalent electronic customs release. Services are zero-rated under Arts. 23 and 24 VAT Act when the place of supply is outside Switzerland, particularly services provided to a foreign recipient in the course of the recipient's business, or services directly connected to exported goods or goods located abroad. For cosmetics e-commerce, export consignments must leave Switzerland via customs-approved parcels and be traceable to the foreign recipient. Swiss law does not set a statutory FX repatriation deadline; administrative practice for export documentation completion is benchmarked at 180 days.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung / déclaration d'exportation) with customs stamp or electronic customs release record
Commercial export invoice prepared in accordance with Swiss VAT invoice requirements
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR, or equivalent transport document showing consignee abroad
Retail sales or delivery record for each export consignment
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing payment from the foreign buyer
Foreign recipient's VAT ID or commercial register extract for offshore B2B services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV and cantonal tax authorities scrutinize export zero-rating claims for completeness and authenticity of documentary evidence. If proof of export is absent or insufficient, the supply is retrospectively taxed at 8.1% with default interest from the original due date. Deliberate misuse, false declarations or forged documentation constitutes VAT evasion under Art. 97 VAT Act, punishable by a fine of up to three times the tax evaded and, in serious cases, criminal penalties including imprisonment. The limitation period for concealed VAT violations is ten years, and any reassessment of exported supplies also triggers reversal of related input VAT credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) — the sole monetary authority; banking supervision and AML/CFT oversight delegated to FINMA (Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority); no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. There are no exchange controls, no restrictions on profit remittances, dividends, interest, or capital repatriation. Dividend distributions to foreign shareholders are subject to Swiss withholding tax of 35%, which may be reduced or refunded under applicable double tax treaties. Cross-border payments are freely effected through regulated banking channels and may be captured in SNB statistical payment reporting, but require no prior regulatory approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no export proceeds surrender or conversion obligation. Export receipts may be retained freely in any currency, held offshore, or converted as desired. Mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; no statutory surrender timeline exists. The only passive requirement is statistical reporting of cross-border payments by the resident bank to the SNB for monetary statistics purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium — offshore digital EMIs may serve only as ancillary payment gateways; they cannot legally execute CHFin clearing or hold customer deposits without a Swiss banking license. Under Art. 1b of the Swiss Banking Act, a fintech license allows FINMA-compliant custodial deposit-taking up to CHF 100 million without full banking licence conditions. An unregulated offshore EMI must route client funds through a licensed Swiss correspondent bank and cannot clear SIC transactions directly. For Shopify/PayPal-based retail, an offshore EMI may collect card proceeds abroad, but all CHF treasury must ultimately be settled via a licensed Swiss bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires directors to appear physically for corporate account opening. FINMA's AML Ordinance and Circular 2022/1 permit remote video identification if conducted through a compliant digital identity (e.g. SwissID) or bank-approved video verification process. However, for a Swiss AG with foreign directors or non-resident shareholders, banks usually require a physical or video interview of the authorised signatories and the independent verification of a corporate resolution and UBO structure. Physical notarisation before a Swiss notary may be required if the bank determines enhanced due diligence is prudent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reported monthly revenue materially inconsistent with Shopify/PayPal settlement volumes, tax filings, or inventory purchasing patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle comprising monthly payment processor payout statements, platform settlement reports, ERP sales ledger, Swiss VAT declarations, commercial tax returns, customs/import invoices for goods, logistics waybills, and a board-approved reconciliation note

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected large inbound or round-trip payments from third-party funding entities located in sanctions-flagged or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle comprising audited financial statements, notarised shareholder resolutions, corporate registry extracts, passport copies and UBO registers, SWIFT MT103 credit evidence with reference strings tying each payment to a specific commercial supply contract, negative sanctions hits from OFAC, SECO, EU and UN lists, and legal counsel letters explaining the commercial substance

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or beneficial-owner reputation flags due to unsettled judgments, prior bankruptcy, or unexplained crypto-asset enrichment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle comprising current commercial register and official debt enforcement extracts, no-bankruptcy certificates, litigation history from reputable legal databases, audited financial statements, crypto-to-fiat exchange statements with electronic identity verification and travel-rule compliance, and professional references from an established Swiss fiduciary or tax adviser

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection by foreign shareholders should be executed as a SWIFT MT103 credit transfer from the foreign bank to the Swiss AG's capital escrow or operating account with the payment reference stating 'Kapitalerhöhung' or 'Einzahlung in Kapitalreserven' (share capital increase or contribution to capital reserve). A notarised board resolution and share register update must be presented to the receiving Swiss bank. If a shareholder loan is used, a full written loan agreement is required. No SNB approval is needed, but the Swiss receiving bank will record the transaction in SNB payment statistics. For amounts in excess of CHF 100,000, banks typically mandate additional source-of-wealth documentation such as bank statements, shareholder financial statements, and signed indemnity letters.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlement may route through SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for CHF-denominated invoices, SEPA for EUR, or SWIFT MT103 for GBP, USD, and other currencies. For high-value cosmetic procurement where credit enhancement is needed, commercial letters of credit (irrevocable, confirmation optional) are issued under ICC UCP600 rules. The standard documentary package includes commercial invoice, port/packing list, certificate of origin, and conforming transport documents. For recurring retail restocking, open account settlement via SWIFT MT103 with full-purpose codes remains the recommended lowest-cost rail. All outbound payments must pass bank name-screening against FINMA sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-currency swaps with a licensed Swiss bank or OECD-authorised dealer
FX swaps for rolling liquidity management

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — permissible only where convention requires USD or EUR settlement due to counterparty restrictions, though the CHF spot/forward market itself is fully onshore convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) approved by the general meeting of shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None (shareholder approval; minutes retained in minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance-sheet date; if fiscal year = calendar year, no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board liability for late approval; shareholders or court may compel meeting; persistent non-compliance can lead to judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return (Steuererklärung / Déclaration fiscale) with attached financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal and municipal tax administrations of the registered office (federal corporate tax assessed within the same return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonal due date generally between 31 March and 30 April for calendar-year companies; automatic or discretionary extensions up to 30 September available on application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties up to 3% of assessed tax, default interest, and estimated assessment based on prior income or assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final VAT return and annual reconciliation (Mehrwertsteuerabrechnung / Déclaration TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the end of each settlement period; annual filers accordingly by 60 days after 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, fines up to CHF 8,000 for filing defaults, and criminal penalties up to CHF 250,000 for intentional evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register audit and confirmation before the annual general meeting (share register, directors register, minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors; the Commercial Register (Handelsregister) only where changes to registered facts arise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing; must be reviewed and updated no later than the date of the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for inaccurate registers; directors' personal liability for breaches; no automatic strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AGM resolution on profit appropriation, discharge of the board, and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Minute book (signed by the chairperson and minute-taker)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the balance-sheet date, unless law permits extension by shareholder consent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of directors; legal challenge of resolutions; in extreme cases, appointment of a special auditor

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit required if two of these thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: balance sheet total CHF 20,000,000; turnover >CHF 40,000,000; 250 full-time employees. Limited review required if two of these thresholds are exceeded: balance sheet total CHF 10,000,000; turnover >CHF 20,000,000; 50 employees. Companies below the limited-review threshold may unanimously waive audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) accounting provisions (art. 957a–962); Swiss GAAP FER for presentation; IFRS or US GAAP permitted and mandatory for listed issuers.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law imposes no annual UBO declaration or notification to the Commercial Register for a non-listed AG. The board must keep the Aktienbuch (share register) current and ensure the ultimate beneficial owner (natural person controlling >25% of capital or votes) is identifiable from the register and internal AMLA file. Annual confirmation is performed as an internal board review prior to the AGM; no external filing is mandated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of shareholder and board meetings)
Accounting records, vouchers, and annual financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000–$25,000 (Swiss limited review or full audit, depending on turnover and size)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate profit tax: 8.5% on after-tax profit (7.83% on pre-tax profit). Combined federal and cantonal/communal headline rate at registered office ranges from approximately 11.9% (Zug) to 21.0% (highest cantons); typical CH_AG for online cosmetics retail seated in Zug or Zurich faces an aggregate rate of 11.9% to 18.2%. Input metadata flags has_sub_tax_distinction=false, but Switzerland de facto imposes bi-level taxation: federal direct tax plus cantonal/communal profit and capital tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income; patent box with up to 90% exemption of qualifying IP income; R&D super-deduction of 150% available under STAF 2020 in most cantons; notional interest deduction (NID) on excess equity in Zug and selected cantons; capital tax relief on equity allocated to participation and patent-box assets. ISIC 4791 online cosmetics retail does not benefit from sector-specific holidays; ordinary trade profits are fully taxable at the combined rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung juristische Personen), which simultaneously serves as the assessment basis for direct federal tax (DBG) and cantonal/communal taxes. Filed electronically through the canton's e-filing portal (e.g., eZug for Zug, ZH Online Tax for Zurich) or the ESTV-supported cantonal platform; the Swiss Federal Tax Administration does not issue or accept a standalone federal corporate return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (assessment period equals the commercial fiscal year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the fiscal year-end per Art. 126 DBG and cantonal implementing law; for calendar-year AGs the cantonal deadline is typically 30 September of the following year; extensions are granted on request if audited financial statements are pending.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered seat, UID (CHE-...) and commercial register number, board members with authorized signatory powers, purpose clause, fiscal year dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Swiss UID and the name of the Swiss tax representative or fiduciary with power of attorney; non-resident shareholders need not be disclosed unless the AG is controlled from abroad, in which case the effective place of management and substance facts must be declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory balance sheet totals with breakdown of fixed assets, current assets, equity, provisions, and liabilities, plus reconciliation of share capital and reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all intercompany balances and shareholder loans precisely; the tax authority tests whether excessive debt is used to strip profit out of Switzerland via hidden equity contributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit before tax, derived from the audited or statutory annual accounts, with turnover itemized by revenue stream including online DTC sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border management fees, royalties, and interest paid to foreign affiliates must be itemized; substantiation documents must be available on request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax reconciliation and adjustments (steuerliche Aufrechnung und Abzug)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs of non-deductible expenses, hidden profit distributions, excessive director remuneration; deductions for participation relief, patent box, R&D super-deduction, and NID; utilization of prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Hidden distributions to non-resident shareholders are reclassified as dividends subject to 35% withholding tax; attach position papers for any aggressive deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the existence and volume of controlled transactions with foreign related parties, plus confirmation of arm's-length pricing and method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a Local File or a simplified transfer-pricing study where annual cross-border intra-group transactions exceed the applicable Swiss threshold; identify the methodology (typically TNMM for e-commerce distribution functions).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable equity capital for cantonal/communal capital tax, being paid-in share capital, statutory reserves, retained earnings, and disclosed reserves at the beginning and end of the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss AG with full non-resident ownership, the book value of intercompany receivables may be included in taxable equity; NID may reduce the effective burden in cantons applying it.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: Verzugsbusse of up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 175 DBG plus cantonal equivalents; where no return is filed, the authority issues an estimated assessment (Ermessensveranlagung) with a practical uplift of 10% to 30% on the assessed tax; late-payment interest accrues at 4.5% per annum without compounding, and procedural fines may multiply for recurring violations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal withholding tax return on dividends (Verrechnungssteuererklärung), filed with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) on the official form and via the ESTV's e-filing system for withholding tax (elektronische Verrechnungssteuererklärung, portal 'e.verrechnungssteuer').
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly, with a return and payment due within 30 days after the end of each calendar quarter in which taxable distributions occurred.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax on dividends distributed must be declared and remitted at 35% of gross distributions within 30 days after the end of the relevant calendar quarter; maximum extension to 60 days upon prior application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of distributions to shareholders in the quarter: gross dividend per transaction, number of shares, amount of 35% withholding tax withheld.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, the full 35% must be withheld and paid regardless of treaty entitlement; relief occurs only through the refund procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder identification, registered/bearer share status, participation percentage, and indication whether the recipient is a beneficial owner or intermediary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the ultimate beneficial owner; a foreign nominee or custodian must provide declarations for AEOI/reporting and for the Swiss refund claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter amounts for which an exemption permit (bewilligte Zahlstelle) applies or for which the shareholder is a Swiss-resident qualifying holding company (0% charge).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No direct exemption at source without an ESTV permit; otherwise the non-resident shareholder must later file Form 82 within the three-year statutory deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Voluntary disclosure of deemed dividends: excessive interest, excessive royalties, fictitious service fees, and shareholder expense recharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If transactions with non-resident related parties are recharacterized as hidden distributions, the 35% tax is assessed retrospectively and immediately due.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit 35% gross dividends: the tax is due together with default interest at 4.5% per annum; separate procedural fines up to CHF 10,000; verrechnungssteuer evasion penalties reach five times the tax at stake and imprisonment up to five years in qualified cases (Art. 70/71 VStG); directors are personally exposed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends paid by the Swiss AG; reduced to 0% for distributions to Swiss-resident qualifying corporate holders with at least 10% participation and no Swiss permanent establishment issue; for DTA-covered foreign shareholders, the 35% is withheld and subsequently refunded by the ESTV to the treaty rate (typically 15% portfolio, 5% for qualifying holdings of 10% or more depending on the treaty; 0% for certain EU/DTA cases).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss paying AG must withhold 35% at source and remit to the ESTV; the foreign beneficial-owner shareholder then claims the DTA reduction by filing Form 82 (Rückerstattungsgesuch) with the FTA within three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid. Required annexes: a valid foreign tax residence certificate (TRC/Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung) issued by the residence tax authority, a beneficial-ownership declaration, proof of shareholding percentage (share register excerpt), and if the participation exceeds 10%, evidence of substance at the shareholder level to satisfy the PPT/LOB safeguard; Swiss payment agents may enter the ESTV authorization procedure to apply the reduced rate at source, but in practice most non-residents use the refund route.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Swiss statutory withholding tax on payments for patents, trademarks, know-how, and other IP licensed by a Swiss AG to foreign related or unrelated payers; most Swiss DTA royalties are 0%. Interest: 0% Swiss withholding tax on ordinary arm's-length interest on commercial and intercompany loans (non-securitized debt); however, interest on Swiss bond-like instruments and money-market paper (Kassenobligationen) is subject to 35% statutory WHT unless the foreign creditor benefits from a DTA exemption. Anti-abuse recharacterization remains a risk: excessive interest or royalties paid to a zero-tax offshore affiliate without substance are reclassified as hidden dividend distributions and suffer 35% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland follows the OECD three-tier documentation standard: Country-by-Country Report is required where the ultimate parent's consolidated revenue reaches CHF 900 million; the ESTV expects a Master File and Local File for Swiss taxpayers with annual turnover of at least CHF 80 million or with intra-group cross-border transactions exceeding CHF 10 million; a simplified Local File (functional and risk analysis) is advisable for small and medium e-commerce AGs with recurring cross-border related-party purchases. Statutory codification of documentation duties is currently under federal legislative process with projected entry into force in 2025; current basis is Art. 58 DBG, Art. 57 DBG, the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, and ESTV circular (Kreisschreiben Nr. 4) on transfer pricing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no formal Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) in the sense of the GCC or BVI regimes, but substance is enforced through (i) the tax-residence test under Art. 50 DBG, which attributes corporate residence to the Austrian? otherwise to the place of effective management in Switzerland; (ii) FTA substance checks applied when issuing tax-residence certificates and processing DTA refunds; (iii) the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test (PPT), which is applied in Swiss tax treaties and denies treaty benefits to letterbox companies; and (iv) case law confirming that an AG without employees, premises, and local decision-making may be treated as a sham for direct tax and withholding tax purposes. For the ISIC 4791 online cosmetics retail AG, demonstrable Swiss substance includes a physical office or fulfillment base, at least one resident director supervising sales operations, and the exercise of management and control in Switzerland for all purchasing, marketing, pricing, and order-processing decisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Direct Federal and Cantonal Corporate Taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally under-reporting online Shopify Payments and PayPal turnover, booking private expenses as business costs, using fictitious supplier invoices, or deliberately omitting taxable income on the corporate tax return, with intent to evade federal or cantonal profit tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The evaded tax is due with interest at 4.5% per annum; a fine of one-third up to one and a half times the evaded tax under Art. 175 DBG is imposed; qualified evasion based on forged or falsified documents (Art. 176 DBG) carries imprisonment of up to three years; cantonal law applies parallel surcharges and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members are jointly and severally liable under Art. 754 CO for the corporate tax deficit where the company is insolvent and the loss results from a breach of their duty of care; criminal convictions bar the director from holding further board positions; in aggravated cross-border cases, Swiss and foreign mutual legal assistance may trigger surrender proceedings, international travel alerts, and precautionary seizures of personal bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to non-resident shareholders without withholding and remitting 35% Swiss withholding tax, or disguising a distribution as a repayment of capital, a management fee, inflated royalty, or excessive interest paid to a related party in a zero-tax jurisdiction without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The 35% tax is assessed on the gross amount with default interest; evasion penalties reach five times the tax evaded (Art. 70 VStG); repeated or high-value evasion is a crime with imprisonment of up to five years under Art. 71 VStG; the FTA may also withdraw the AG's eligibility for simplified payment procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are answerable to the ESTV for the unimpeded 35% tax when the corporate payer is unable to pay and the default is attributable to their omission; willful personal concealment triggers criminal liability and the potential freezing of personal Swiss bank accounts; foreign travel bans are routinely ordered while the criminal investigation is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unpaid Employer Social Security Contributions (AHV/IV/EO/ALV and BVG)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying employees of the Swiss e-commerce operation off the books, under-declaring wage totals, classifying employees as self-employed service providers to avoid employer contributions, or failing to remit the employer and employee social security shares to the Swiss compensation office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The outstanding AHV/IV/EO/ALV contributions are recovered with arrears interest; additional administrative surcharges apply; criminal sanctions under Art. 87 AHVG include monetary penalties of up to CHF 30,000 and, in cases of fraudulent conduct, deprivation of liberty; the company may also be debarred from public procurement and lose its tax clearance certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Art. 12 AHVG the directors and the liquidator are personally liable for unpaid employer social security contributions, even after liquidation; personal assets of board members can be executed directly; flight risk or asset disposal abroad leads to Swiss travel bans, arrest warrants, and extradition based on social security fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Structure and Abuse of Treaty Benefits (PPT/LOB)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a mailbox Zug AG with no premises, no employees, and no board activity while booking the entire cosmetics retail margin to a zero-tax or tax-haven procurement or IP-holding entity; the Swiss AG acts only as a pass-through invoice company with no management function, risk, or substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authorities re-attribute the profits to the place of effective management and assess federal, cantonal, and communal tax at the full combined rate with default interest; treaty benefits are denied under the PPT, causing the 35% Swiss withholding tax to remain in full; hidden distributions reclassified from the excessive intercompany payments suffer the 35% WHT plus penalties; the company loses access to cantonal privileged regimes and NID.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face qualified tax-evasion prosecution for the artificially created tax advantage, including imprisonment up to three years; personal restitution claims from the tax authorities and minority shareholders under Art. 754 CO can strip board members of personal assets; the Federal Tax Authority may initiate criminal proceedings with travel restrictions and, in severe cases, issue an international arrest warrant through Interpol for the principal director.
